problem:
Find the point(s) of the intersection of the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ and the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=-t \\ y=\sqrt{2}t, \\ z=t+2\end{aligned}$ where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
worked_solution:
Substituting the expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ from the parametric equation of the line into the equation of the sphere, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =4 \\ {(-t)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}t)}^{2}+{(t+2)}^{2} & =4 \\ {t}^{2}+2{t}^{2}+({t}^{2}+4t+4) & =4 \\ 4{t}^{2}+4t+4 & =4 \\ 4{t}^{2}+4t & =0 \\ t(t+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=-1$ and $t=0.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=-1$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-(-1)=1 \\ y=\sqrt{2}(-1)=-\sqrt{2} \\ z=(-1)+2=1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(1,-\sqrt{2},1).$

- For $t=0$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=(0)=0 \\ y=\sqrt{2}(0)=0 \\ z=(0)+2=2,\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(0,0,2).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(1,-\sqrt{2},1)$ and $(0,0,2).$
